paragraphs: CIP Software sells Plan-It, capital planning software written with local government users in mind. The pitch is simple: take the capital improvement planning process off spreadsheets. The people it is aimed at are finance directors, administrators, clerks, public works directors and other city officials across North America.

Departments submit capital requests through web-based forms that upload straight into the agency's own Plan-It database, replacing paper forms and spreadsheets. Once the data is centralized, a plan can be rolled from one year to the next in a click. Reporting is where the company puts its emphasis, offering hundreds of automatically generated and customizable reports.

Plan-It was created in 1998 by founder Bill Leskee, who had run into the same problem building capital improvement plans. Its first municipal installations followed in 1999. Leskee has since retired and handed the company to a new team. The company says it has focused on the capital improvement planning process for more than 25 years. Alongside municipalities, the site names universities and libraries among the organizations that use it. One testimonial on the site is attributed to a finance director in Waterloo, Iowa.
